subject: Mid-sprint readout: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking (baselines, risks, asks)
related_links: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/ (Eng Serving Runtime > Benchmarking and Perf Suite)
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Gupta <neha.gupta@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Mid-sprint readout: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking (baselines, risks, asks)
Attachments: FP8-INT8 Mid-sprint readout (Oct 3) - v3.pdf; fp8_int8_benchmark_matrix_snapshot_2025-10-03.csv

Ava, Neha,

Quick mid-sprint readout from the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint (week 1.5). We have baseline numbers in-hand for A100/H100 and partial for L40S; H200 is gated on lab capacity.

TL;DR
- FP8 on H100 looks promising for decode-heavy traffic (cost-per-token down), but we found a long-context prefill regression we’re actively debugging.
- INT8 path is stable in most shapes, but we hit a kernel auto-selection mismatch that can silently fall back to FP16 for certain INT8 shapes (perf + predictability issue). Fix is in progress.
- We need two things this week: (1) guaranteed perf-lab capacity for H200 + L40S runs, (2) release gating support so we can safely ship the “good” wins without repeating SUP-6193.

Baseline findings (Week 1 baselines; more detail in attached deck)
1) End-to-end serving (hosted-ish traffic shapes)
- H100: FP8 decode-heavy workloads show consistent throughput gains vs FP16 baselines, with TPOT improving materially. TTFT is flat-to-slightly improved when prefill lengths are modest.
- A100: FP8 benefits are smaller and more variable depending on prompt length distribution; kernel selection matters more.
- L40S: early read suggests INT8 can be good, but we have intermittent correctness failures tied to one fused op (we can guard/disable per SKU).

2) Microbench
- FP8 attention kernels: strong on H100 when shapes match tuned tiles; performance cliff shows up on long-context prefill when alignment/stride assumptions break.
- INT8 GEMM: the conversion overhead dominates some shapes; fusing dequant + reducing conversions is the most likely near-term win.

Top risks / watch items
- FP8 long-context prefill regression: impacts TTFT for our “prefill-heavy” prompt set; we can’t recommend default enablement until fixed.
- INT8 silent fallback to FP16 for certain shapes: causes customer-visible regressions because the expected INT8 economics don’t materialize (likely contributor to SUP-6193 symptoms).
- Perf lab variability: noisy runs if we don’t get isolated nodes / pinned clocks. Without consistent lab conditions, the report won’t be defensible.

What we plan to ship vs hold
- Ship (if gates pass):
  - Kernel selection / logging improvements + guardrails (so we can explain perf deltas and avoid mismatched auto-selection).
  - Low-risk conversion overhead reductions in INT8 GEMM.
  - Scheduler batch-size cap override for quantized decode to reduce p95/p99 tails under mixed prompt lengths.
- Hold (until fixed):
  - FP8 default-on for long-context prefill-heavy routes.

Asks
1) Perf-lab capacity (blocking)
- We need reserved access for 2–3 days next week on H200 + L40S nodes to complete the matrix and re-run after fixes.
- Request: prioritize/approve INT-842 so SRE can isolate nodes and stop background contention during the benchmark window.

2) Release gating support (to avoid customer repeats)
- We need Connor + release eng to help us integrate quant benchmarks into perf-canary with explicit thresholds + allowlists (block release if TTFT/TPOT regress beyond policy).
- Request: align that quant perf gating is “release blocking” for the affected routes/models once we have baselines (not best-effort). This is the only way we can ship kernel/scheduler changes with confidence.

If helpful, I can do a 15 min walk-through in staff today. Otherwise, we’ll keep driving and update again once H200 results are in.

Mateo
Executive Sponsor, Runtime
Redwood Inference


---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Gupta <neha.gupta@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 11:04 AM PT
Subject: Re: Mid-sprint readout: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking (baselines, risks, asks)

Thanks Mateo.

On gating: I agree we should make this release-blocking for the quantized paths that are enabled by default (or likely to be enabled soon). The tricky part is we need stable baselines and a small “allowed variance” band for the lab noise.

Two questions so I can set expectations with Release Train:
1) Which exact E2E scenarios do you want as the gating minimum (streaming chat TTFT/TPOT + one non-streaming throughput case?), and which models are “must cover”?
2) Do we have a clear policy for correctness drift failures on L40S (block vs GPU-conditional disable)?

If we can answer those today, I’ll get Sahana to help wire it into perf-canary and make sure the release checklist references it.

Also +1 on INT-842. If Sean can reserve nodes for 48–72 hrs, we can avoid the churn we’ve seen in the nightly jobs.

Connor
Release Engineering


---

From: Neha Gupta <neha.gupta@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 1:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Mid-sprint readout: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking (baselines, risks, asks)

This is helpful.

Re: INT-842 — I’m supportive, but I want a crisp “why now” note for infra since they’re triaging multiple perf-lab requests.

Mateo: can you reply with (a) which deliverable is blocked without H200/L40S runs and (b) what’s the minimum reservation window (hours/day) to be successful? Please keep it scoped so Sean can say yes.

Connor: for gating, I’d prefer we start with a narrow set of must-pass tests rather than a large matrix that will flake. Suggest:
- Streaming chat scenario (TTFT + TPOT) on H100 and A100 for 2–3 top models
- One long-context prefill-heavy scenario explicitly to catch the FP8 regression class
- Correctness drift checks for INT8/FP8 vs FP16 baseline on the same prompt set

On the L40S intermittent correctness: GPU-conditional disable is acceptable if we have a clean detection + documented caveat, but I don’t want a situation where we “pass” gates while a SKU is broken silently. It needs to be explicit in the release notes and in runtime logging.

Neha


---

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Gupta <neha.gupta@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 2:57 PM PT
Subject: Re: Mid-sprint readout: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking (baselines, risks, asks)

+1 to both asks.

Mateo — please send the short “why now / what’s blocked” note Neha requested and include an explicit tie to customer risk (SUP-6193 / SUP-6194) and why gating is necessary.

Connor — proceed with a minimal gating plan this release train. If the numbers are noisy, we’d rather tighten methodology (pinned containers, clocks, node isolation) than waive gates.

Also: do not enable FP8 defaults broadly until the long-context TTFT issue is resolved and we’ve shown no quality regressions on the sanity eval set.

Ava
